title: The Straw Hats for the Jizo
text:
A poor old couple lived in a mountain village in Japan. On the last day of the year they had nothing in the house with which to celebrate the New Year, not even a few rice cakes. So the old man took five straw hats that he had woven and set out through the snow to sell them in town.

Nobody in the market wanted to buy hats. As evening came on, the old man trudged home with all five, the snow falling ever thicker.

On the way he passed a row of six stone Jizo statues standing by the road, the guardian figures that watch over travelers and children. Their heads and shoulders were covered with snow. The old man felt sorry for them. He brushed off the snow and tied a straw hat on each one. When he came to the sixth, there was no hat left, so he took off his own head cloth and tied it on the last statue.

At home he told his wife what he had done, and instead of scolding him, she said he had done well. They went to bed hungry. In the night they heard voices singing and something heavy being dragged through the snow. In the morning they found rice, rice cakes, vegetables and treasures piled at their door, and six Jizo, wearing hats, walking away into the distance.
lesson: The kindness that matters most is often given when you have little to spare. Small gestures to those who cannot repay you are never wasted.
people: A poor old couple, six Jizo statues
